recipes.name: Fluffy Gingerbread Pancakes
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup butter, melted and cooled to lukewarm

steps.text: Whisk together the milk, coffee, butter, and eggs in a bowl until evenly blended; set aside. In a large bowl, stir together the all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and cloves; pour the egg mixture into the flour mixture, and stir just until combined. Set aside for 10 to 15 minutes.

Coat the bottom of a large skillet with cooking spray, and place pan over medium heat. Scoop large spoonfuls of batter onto the hot pan, and fry until bubbles appear on the surface. Flip and cook until browned on the other side. Continue with remaining batter.

raw_recipe.headline: Fluffy Gingerbread Pancakes
raw_recipe.description: Light, fluffy pancakes that taste like gingerbread! Great for the holidays!

review.reviewBody: After having Gingerbread pancakes at a national chain breakfast house, I simply HAD to find the recipe online. I made this recipe with no changes and my husband and children ate every one of them. My husband even commented that he liked this recipe better than the restaurant's! This is one we will be making over and over.

I reduced butter and halved the dry ingredients while keeping the wet ingredients the same. Then was able to add as much of the wet ingredients as I wanted for a consistency I like. Pancakes were awesome and the leftovers in the toaster oven 1/2 week later with my coffee were Devine. Yummy.

Very good! I completely cut out the butter and used half the brown sugar and it was excellent. Even my sister liked it and she made it exactly the way the recipe called for so I know she didn't even miss the butter or extra sugar. I made the batter the night before so the seasonings had time to meld togther. I froze the leftovers and reheated in the toaster and it was even better. Plus the extra crispiness from the toasted helped the pancakes from being to soggy. The mixture of seasonings is wonderful. Thanks for posting this recipe.

Let me start off by saying this smells sooo good and taste pretty good too, however the batter was so thick and hard to work with that I decided the forget the pancakes and make so really good muffins.
If you like a thick pancake leave as is. I just watered down the batter a bit so they were thinner. Amazing! Perfect for the season.

I had gingerbread pancakes in a restaurant in Texas and have wanted them ever since. Finally did it and sad I waited so long. Delicious and easy. I had all the ingredients in my kitchen. That’s a miracle. Thanks for sharing.

Very nice flavor! Not too strong...I was worried that gingerbread pancakes would have too overwhelming a taste to eat more than half a pancake, but these were very pleasant. My family devoured them, and requested that I make them again!
These are so good and i made them and me and my sister ate them and now she want some more but i dont fill like making some but i told her ill make some in the morning.
Flavor was OK but not something I would call gingerbread, more like spice cake. It was definitely more like muffin mix than pancake batter, was WAY too thick. Too sweet, too cakey.
Flavor was OK but not something I would call gingerbread, more like spice cake. It was definitely more like muffin mix than pancake batter, was WAY too thick. Too sweet, too cakey.

These were alright. I would suggest you try them out but I will keep searching. I found them to be a little dry, despite the entire stick of butter. I didn't over cook them either. My 8 year old requested more gingerbread flavor.
Without a doubt the best gingerbread pancake recipe we've tried. I didn't change a thing.
